newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firmer, Wall St seen key to growth.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firmer, Wall St seen key to growth.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose in morning trade after four days of holidays, buoyed by investor optimism after Wall Street's surge on Friday, traders said.
But they said further short-term growth, though possible, would depend on Western demand.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares opened at 322.14 after closing last Wednesday at 321.19.

"If America turns out to be the locomotive in this direction, investors will try to buy a little bit more in Russia. It's clear now that it's smart to buy here," said Dmitry Starenko, senior trader at Regent European Securities.
The Dow Jones closed up 94.72 points on Friday at 7071.21
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2700 at 1010 GMT from $0.2600 at Wednesday's close, while regional energy utility Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS edged up to $0.281 from $0.246.
International long-distance telephone company Rostelekom RTKM.RTS firmed to $3.87 from $3.80.
But traders said a correction was possible since the market rise was also serving to moderate the optimism of operators who were looking to see whether Western orders would show up later in the day.

"The situation on the market is very unbalanced: everybody's worrying and waiting to see if orders will come in. If it's just speculation again then a correction is possible," said Dmitry Yevenko, head of securities trading at UCB.
